conformanceOverview.conformanceSummary: Thorium Reader Desktop provides comprehensive access to assistive technologies and offers a variety of customisation options for content display and interface behaviour. In many cases, it meets the Level AAA criteria. However, there are certain limitations: the lack of a zoom function for the interface can detract from the reading experience, and some specialised features have not yet been tested.

rules.title: Non-text Content
rules.notes: all visual information is also available as text
rules.description: All non-text content that is presented to the user has a text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose.

rules.title: Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)
rules.notes: Thorium Reader can restitue publications with pre-recorded audio or video.
rules.description: Either an alternative for time-based media or an audio track is provided that presents equivalent information for prerecorded video-only content.

rules.title: Captions (Prerecorded)
rules.notes: Thorium Reader can restitue publications with pre-recorded captions.
rules.description: Captions are provided for all prerecorded audio content in synchronized media, except when the media is a media alternative for text and is clearly labeled as such.

rules.title: Captions (Live)
rules.notes: Live captions may be available depending on the video-service provided by the ebook creator.
rules.description: Captions are provided for all live audio content in synchronized media.

rules.title: Audio Description (Prerecorded)
rules.notes: Thorium Reader can restitue publications with pre-recorded Audio descriptions.
rules.description: Audio description is provided for all prerecorded video content in synchronized media.

rules.title: Sign Language (Prerecorded)
rules.notes: Thorium Reader can restitue publications with pre-recorded Sign language videos. An experimental feature allows the reading of authored-synchronisation between text and video.
rules.description: Sign language interpretation is provided for all prerecorded audio content in synchronized media.

rules.title: Extended Audio Description (Prerecorded)
rules.notes: Thorium Reader can restitue publications with pre-recorded extended audio descriptions.
rules.description: Where pauses in foreground audio are insufficient to allow audio descriptions to convey the sense of the video, extended audio description is provided for all prerecorded video content in synchronized media.

rules.title: Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
rules.notes: Thorium Reader can restitue publications with pre-recorded media alternative.
rules.description: An alternative for time-based media is provided for all prerecorded synchronized media and for all prerecorded video-only media.

rules.title: Audio-only (Live)
rules.notes: Thorium Reader can restitue publications with live-audio only, depending of the streaming application chosen and implemented by the ebook-creator.
rules.description: An alternative for time-based media that presents equivalent information for live audio-only content is provided.

rules.title: Info and Relationships
rules.notes: Thorium Reader makes use of HTML markup with additional ARIA roles when necessary. It also fully restitues all XHTML and ARIA markup as authored in publications.
rules.description: Information, structure, and relationships conveyed through presentation can be programmatically determined or are available in text.

rules.title: Meaningful Sequence
rules.description: When the sequence in which content is presented affects its meaning, a correct reading sequence can be programmatically determined.

rules.title: Sensory Characteristics
rules.description: Instructions provided for understanding and operating content do not rely solely on sensory characteristics of components such as shape, color, size, visual location, orientation, or sound.

rules.title: Orientation
rules.description: Content does not restrict its view and operation to a single display orientation, such as portrait or landscape, unless a specific display orientation is essential.

rules.title: Identify Input Purpose
rules.description: The purpose of each input field collecting information about the user can be programmatically determined when the input field serves a purpose identified in the Input Purposes for user interface components section.

rules.title: Identify Purpose
rules.description: In content implemented using markup languages, the purpose of user interface components, icons, and regions can be programmatically determined.

rules.title: Use of Color
rules.description: Color is not used as the only visual means of conveying information, indicating an action, prompting a response, or distinguishing a visual element.

rules.title: Audio Control
rules.description: If any audio on a web page plays automatically for more than 3 seconds, either a mechanism is available to pause or stop the audio, or a mechanism is available to control audio volume independently from the overall system volume level.

rules.title: Contrast (Minimum)
rules.description: The visual presentation of text and images of text has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1, except for large text (3:1), incidental, or logotypes.

rules.title: Resize text
rules.notes: The text from the interface cannot be resized.
rules.description: Except for captions and images of text, text can be resized without assistive technology up to 200 percent without loss of content or functionality.

rules.title: Images of Text
rules.description: If the technologies being used can achieve the visual presentation, text is used to convey information rather than images of text except for customizable or essential cases.

rules.title: Contrast (Enhanced)
rules.description: The visual presentation of text and images of text has a contrast ratio of at least 7:1, except for large text (4.5:1), incidental, or logotypes.

rules.title: Low or No Background Audio
rules.description: For prerecorded audio-only content that contains primarily speech in the foreground, is not an audio CAPTCHA or audio logo, and is not vocalization intended to be primarily musical expression such as singing or rapping, at least one of the following is true: no background, turn off, or 20 dB.

rules.title: Visual Presentation
rules.description: For the visual presentation of blocks of text, a mechanism is available to achieve the following: foreground and background colors can be selected, width is no more than 80 characters or glyphs, text is not justified, line spacing is at least space-and-a-half within paragraphs, paragraph spacing is at least 1.5 times larger than line spacing, and text can be resized without assistive technology up to 200 percent.

rules.title: Images of Text (No Exception)
rules.description: Images of text are only used for pure decoration or where a particular presentation of text is essential to the information being conveyed.

rules.title: Reflow
rules.notes: The text from the interface cannot be resized.
rules.description: Content can be presented without loss of information or functionality, and without requiring scrolling in two dimensions for vertical scrolling content at 320 CSS pixels width or horizontal scrolling content at 256 CSS pixels height.

rules.title: Non-text Contrast
rules.description: The visual presentation of user interface components and graphical objects has a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against adjacent color(s).

rules.title: Text Spacing
rules.description: In content implemented using markup languages that support the following text style properties, no loss of content or functionality occurs by setting line height to at least 1.5 times the font size, spacing following paragraphs to at least 2 times the font size, letter spacing to at least 0.12 times the font size, and word spacing to at least 0.16 times the font size.

rules.title: Content on Hover or Focus
rules.description: Where receiving and then removing pointer hover or keyboard focus triggers additional content to become visible and then hidden, the following are true: dismissible, hoverable, persistent.

rules.title: Keyboard
rules.description: All functionality of the content is operable through a keyboard interface without requiring specific timings for individual keystrokes, except where the underlying function requires input that depends on the path of the user's movement and not just the endpoints.

rules.title: No Keyboard Trap
rules.description: If keyboard focus can be moved to a component of the page using a keyboard interface, then focus can be moved away from that component using only a keyboard interface, and, if it requires more than unmodified arrow or tab keys or other standard exit methods, the user is advised of the method for moving focus away.

rules.title: Keyboard (No Exception)
rules.description: All functionality of the content is operable through a keyboard interface without requiring specific timings for individual keystrokes.

rules.title: Character Key Shortcuts
rules.description: If a keyboard shortcut is implemented in content using only letter (including upper- and lower-case letters), punctuation, number, or symbol characters, then at least one of the following is true: turn off, remap, or active only on focus.

rules.title: Timing Adjustable
rules.description: For each time limit that is set by the content, at least one of the following is true: turn off, adjust, extend, real-time exception, essential exception, or 20 hour exception.

rules.title: Pause, Stop, Hide
rules.description: For moving, blinking, scrolling, or auto-updating information, a mechanism for the user to pause, stop, or hide it is available unless the movement is part of an activity where it is essential.

rules.title: No Timing
rules.description: Timing is not an essential part of the event or activity presented by the content, except for non-interactive synchronized media and real-time events.

rules.title: Interruptions
rules.description: Interruptions can be postponed or suppressed by the user, except interruptions involving an emergency.

rules.title: Re-authenticating
rules.description: When an authenticated session expires, the user can continue the activity without loss of data after re-authenticating.

rules.title: Timeouts
rules.description: Users are warned of the duration of any user inactivity that could cause data loss, unless the data is preserved for more than 20 hours when the user does not take any actions.

rules.title: Three Flashes or Below Threshold
rules.description: Web pages do not contain anything that flashes more than three times in any one second period, or the flash is below the general flash and red flash thresholds.

rules.title: Three Flashes
rules.description: Web pages do not contain anything that flashes more than three times in any one second period.

rules.title: Animation from Interactions
rules.description: Motion animation triggered by interaction can be disabled, unless the animation is essential to the functionality or information being conveyed.

rules.title: Bypass Blocks
rules.description: A mechanism is available to bypass blocks of content that are repeated on multiple web pages.

rules.title: Page Titled
rules.description: Web pages have titles that describe topic or purpose.

rules.title: Focus Order
rules.description: If a web page can be navigated sequentially and the navigation sequences affect meaning or operation, focusable components receive focus in an order that preserves meaning and operability.

rules.title: Link Purpose (In Context)
rules.description: The purpose of each link can be determined from the link text alone or from the link text together with its programmatically determined link context, except where the purpose of the link would be ambiguous to users in general.

rules.title: Multiple Ways
rules.description: More than one way is available to locate a web page within a set of web pages except where the web page is the result of, or a step in, a process.

rules.title: Headings and Labels
rules.description: Headings and labels describe topic or purpose.

rules.title: Focus Visible
rules.description: Any keyboard operable user interface has a mode of operation where the keyboard focus indicator is visible.

rules.title: Location
rules.description: Information about the user's location within a set of web pages is available.

rules.title: Link Purpose (Link Only)
rules.description: A mechanism is available to allow the purpose of each link to be identified from link text alone, except where the purpose of the link would be ambiguous to users in general.

rules.title: Section Headings
rules.description: Section headings are used to organize the content.

rules.title: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
rules.description: When a user interface component receives keyboard focus, the component is not entirely hidden behind author-created content.

rules.title: Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced)
rules.description: When a user interface component receives keyboard focus, no part of the component is hidden behind author-created content.

rules.title: Focus Appearance
rules.description: When the keyboard focus indicator is visible, an area of the focus indicator meets the following: is at least as large as the area of a 2 CSS pixel thick perimeter of the unfocused component or sub-component, and has a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 between the same pixels in the focused and unfocused states.

rules.title: Pointer Gestures
rules.description: All functionality that uses multipoint or path-based gestures for operation can be operated with a single pointer without a path-based gesture, unless a multipoint or path-based gesture is essential.

rules.title: Pointer Cancellation
rules.description: For functionality that can be operated using a single pointer, at least one of the following is true: no down-event, abort or undo, up reversal, or essential.

rules.title: Label in Name
rules.description: For user interface components with labels that include text or images of text, the name contains the text that is presented visually.

rules.title: Target Size (Enhanced)
rules.description: The size of the target for pointer inputs is at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels except when equivalent, inline, user agent control, or essential.

rules.title: Concurrent Input Mechanisms
rules.description: Web content does not restrict use of input modalities available on a platform except where the restriction is essential, required to ensure the security of the content, or required to respect user settings.

rules.title: Dragging Movements
rules.description: All functionality that uses a dragging movement for operation can be achieved by a single pointer without dragging, unless dragging is essential or the functionality is determined by the user agent and not modified by the author.

rules.title: Target Size (Minimum)
rules.description: The size of the target for pointer inputs is at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, except when spacing, equivalent, inline, user agent control, or essential.

rules.title: Language of Page
rules.description: The default human language of each web page can be programmatically determined.

rules.title: Language of Parts
rules.description: The human language of each passage or phrase in the content can be programmatically determined except for proper names, technical terms, words of indeterminate language, and words or phrases that have become part of the vernacular of the immediately surrounding text.

rules.title: Unusual Words
rules.notes: There is an ongoing discussion about Dictionary Integration in Thorium Reader
rules.description: A mechanism is available for identifying specific definitions of words or phrases used in an unusual or restricted way, including idioms and jargon.

rules.title: Abbreviations
rules.notes: If the abbr tag is present in a puiblication, it will be rendered as a tooltip and made available to assistive technologies.
rules.description: A mechanism for identifying the expanded form or meaning of abbreviations is available.

rules.title: Reading Level
rules.description: When text requires reading ability more advanced than the lower secondary education level after removal of proper names and titles, supplemental content, or a version that does not require reading ability more advanced than the lower secondary education level, is available.

rules.title: Pronunciation
rules.description: A mechanism is available for identifying specific pronunciation of words where meaning of the words, in context, is ambiguous without knowing the pronunciation.

rules.title: On Focus
rules.description: When any user interface component receives focus, it does not initiate a change of context.

rules.title: On Input
rules.description: Changing the setting of any user interface component does not automatically cause a change of context unless the user has been advised of the behavior before using the component.

rules.title: Consistent Navigation
rules.description: Navigational mechanisms that are repeated on multiple web pages within a set of web pages occur in the same relative order each time they are repeated, unless a change is initiated by the user.

rules.title: Consistent Identification
rules.description: Components that have the same functionality within a set of web pages are identified consistently.

rules.title: Change on Request
rules.description: Changes of context are initiated only by user request or a mechanism is available to turn off such changes.

rules.title: Consistent Help
rules.description: If a web page contains any help mechanisms, and those mechanisms are repeated on multiple web pages within a set of web pages, they occur in the same order relative to other page content, unless a change is initiated by the user.

rules.title: Error Identification
rules.description: If an input error is automatically detected, the item that is in error is identified and the error is described to the user in text.

rules.title: Labels or Instructions
rules.description: Labels or instructions are provided when content requires user input.

rules.title: Error Suggestion
rules.description: If an input error is automatically detected and suggestions for correction are known, then the suggestions are provided to the user, unless it would jeopardize the security or purpose of the content.

rules.title: Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data)
rules.description: For web pages that cause legal commitments or financial transactions for the user to occur, that modify or delete user-controllable data in data storage systems, or that submit user test responses, at least one of the following is true: reversible, checked, or confirmed.

rules.title: Help
rules.description: Context-sensitive help is available.

rules.title: Error Prevention (All)
rules.description: For web pages that require the user to submit information, at least one of the following is true: reversible, checked, or confirmed.

rules.title: Redundant Entry
rules.description: Information previously entered by or provided to the user that is required to be entered again in the same process is either auto-populated, or available for the user to select.

rules.title: Accessible Authentication
rules.description: A cognitive function test is not required for any step in an authentication process unless that step provides at least one of the following: alternative, mechanism, object recognition, or personal content.

rules.title: Accessible Authentication (No Exception)
rules.description: A cognitive function test is not required for any step in an authentication process unless that step provides at least one of the following: alternative or mechanism.

rules.title: Name, Role, Value
rules.description: For all user interface components, the name and role can be programmatically determined; states, properties, and values that can be set by the user can be programmatically set; and notification of changes to these items is available to user agents, including assistive technologies.

rules.title: Status Messages
rules.description: In content implemented using markup languages, status messages can be programmatically determined through role or properties such that they can be presented to the user by assistive technologies without receiving focus.
